limitations: These are direct-helper complete lifecycle timings; Oxlint and its final JSON formatter are excluded. Output goes to regular files.
macOS hardware instruction counts are local measurements, not deterministic Linux bench/count.py results.
Fresh process per sample, warm filesystem, default thread overrides cleared; no builds, tests or other benchmarks overlap these timed runs.

Controls have one observation per cell and use GOMAXPROCS=1 RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1; the new compiler still uses its parallel loader algorithm with a one-worker pool unless singleThreaded is set in configuration.
Rust and installed Go retain known compiler/rule-version differences. Go diagnostic counts can vary; before/after Rust multisets remain exact.

Do not compare absolute times across earlier sessions; use paired comparisons within each publish. Setup removes all rules and compiler diagnostics but still includes discovery, loading, binding and teardown.
